XP granted per completed voice interval.

Maximum XP granted for a qualifying message; must be greater than or equal to the minimum.
Minimum XP granted for a qualifying message.

defaults.rationale: Gentle early levels for quick wins, meaningful grind at high levels; fully owner-tunable.
No reward roles until the owner defines them; announcements activate per binding.
Levels reward genuine activity out of the box; visible status is core to the community experience.
No exclusion role until the owner assigns one.
Voice regulars deserve status too; both activity types count by default.
Five-minute intervals smooth accrual and survive brief disconnects.
Steady voice accrual roughly comparable to relaxed chatting.
No channels scoped until the owner opts in to allowlist or denylist mode.
Rich open default: every channel counts until the owner scopes it.
One-minute anti-spam cooldown rewards conversation, not flooding.
Highest-wins is the least surprising combination rule and prevents runaway stacking.
Small random spread keeps accrual organic without enabling spam races.
Industry-familiar floor that makes every genuine message feel worthwhile.

defaults.rationale: Blackjack rewards skill and can double down, so it ships with a modestly higher default cap than the pure-chance games while staying conservative.
The casino floor is a flagship game-economy draw and ships on for the maximal out-of-box experience; owners can switch it off in one click.
A conservative default table limit keeps early wagers small and losses recoverable; owners raise it freely as their economy matures.
A sane non-zero daily loss ceiling protects members from grinding their whole wallet away in one session while leaving plenty of room for a fun run; owners can raise, lower, or disable it.
Slots swing hard on a jackpot symbol, so the default cap matches the conservative coinflip limit to keep variance friendly for casual players.

domains.name: Casino Games of Chance

permissions.action: Wager from or receive a payout into another member's play-money wallet
permissions.actor: Any guild member
permissions.enforcement: Every economy_add_balance and economy_subtract_balance call is keyed to the invoking member's own guild and user id; no code path debits or credits another member's wallet from a casino command.

permissions.action: Edit casino settings (enable flag, per-game wager caps, daily loss cap) on the dashboard economy games page

permissions.action: Convert casino play-money winnings into real-store credit, commerce entitlements, or any real-money value
permissions.actor: Any actor
permissions.enforcement: The casino reads and writes only economy_wallets and economy_daily_losses; there is no code path from a casino payout to the commerce or billing tables, and commerce-held roles grant no casino income.

permissions.action: Run /coinflip, /slots, /roulette, /blackjack, /dice, /rps, /scratch, /guess, and the free /highlow
permissions.actor: Any guild member
permissions.enforcement: Casino slash commands respond for every member; each bet only ever mutates the invoking member's own economy_wallets row, and a per-user Valkey lock (SET NX PX, fail-closed) permits at most one in-flight bet per member.

domains.promise: Members wager play-money coins across the full advertised casino floor — coinflip, slots, roulette, blackjack, dice, rock-paper-scissors, scratch cards, guess-the-number, and the free high-low — with every outcome drawn from the project CSPRNG for uniform, tamper-resistant fairness. Owner-configurable per-game wager caps and a per-member daily loss cap keep stakes real but recoverable, a per-user lock makes concurrent bets safe, and losses are tracked in a restart-durable daily counter. It is all the fake game economy forever: no bet, payout, or jackpot ever touches real money, casino winnings are never convertible to the real paid store, and commerce-held roles earn no casino income.

controls.description: Number of farm plots per member (guild_config.economy_farm_grid_size); the bot renders a square-ceiling grid and refuses new plants once every plot is occupied.
Master switch for farming (guild_config.economy_farming_enabled); when off, growth and harvest stop resolving and /farm commands explain the feature is disabled.
Whether unharvested crops spoil (guild_config.economy_farming_wilt_enabled); when on, a crop left past its harvest window wilts to nothing and the plot becomes reclaimable.
Percentage the grow timer is cut when a plot is fertilized (guild_config.economy_fertilizer_time_reduction_pct); applied once per fertilized plot.

defaults.rationale: A nine-plot (3x3) grid gives quick early wins with room to grow into a long-term farm without overwhelming casual members.
Farming is a flagship idle game-economy loop and ships on for the maximal out-of-box experience; owners can switch it off at any time.
Real-but-recoverable stakes: unharvested crops can spoil so harvest windows carry weight, but a wilted plot is simply reclaimable — never a play-coin loss.
Fertilizer halving grow time is a satisfying, deep-config lever owners can tune anywhere from 0 to 100 percent.

domains.promise: Members grow crops on a persistent, per-guild farm grid: /farm plant seeds an empty plot, /farm water starts its growth timer, fertilizer cuts that timer, and /farm harvest sells matured crops for play-money coins while returning seeds — with crops spoiling if left past their harvest window when wilt is enabled. Every plot's crop, growth timer, fertilizer flag, and spoilage state survives a full stack restart. Every seed, crop, coin, and fertilizer here is play-money game inventory inside the fake economy: nothing is bought with real money, farmed goods are never real-money market-sellable, and commerce-granted roles earn no farm income.

controls.description: Play-money coin bonus paid exactly once when a member discovers every active species in the guild catch table.
Whether completing the full per-member species collection pays a one-time play-money bonus; when off, collections still fill and display but the completion bonus is not paid.
Seconds a member must wait between successful casts, backed by economy_fishing_cooldown_seconds and enforced by an atomic Valkey SET NX claim keyed to guild and user.
Master switch for fishing, backed by the economy_fishing_enabled guild_config key; when off, /fish subcommands explain the feature is disabled and no catch is recorded.
Percent chance a cast pulls up junk (old boot, seaweed, tin can) instead of a fish, backed by economy_fishing_junk_chance_pct; junk plus treasure must not exceed 100.
Percent chance a cast surfaces a treasure chest (ancient coin, pearl, golden ring) paying bonus play coins, backed by economy_fishing_treasure_chance_pct; junk plus treasure must not exceed 100.

defaults.rationale: A meaningful but recoverable play-coin bonus that honors the grind of discovering every species; fully owner-tunable.
The completion bonus rewards long-term mastery and ships on; owners can switch the piece off independently.
A gentle 30-second pace keeps casting rewarding and grindy without letting a member farm coins in a tight loop.
Fishing is a flagship casual game-economy loop and ships on for the maximal out-of-box experience.
A modest 15 percent junk rate adds variety and quick early wins without souring the catch feel.
A rare 5 percent treasure chance gives an occasional exciting payout while keeping the sum well under 100.

controls.description: Seconds a member must wait between gathers of the same source (guild_config.economy_gathering_cooldown_seconds), enforced atomically per member and source via a Valkey SET PX NX lock.
Master switch for gathering (guild_config.economy_gathering_enabled); when off, /hunt, /dig, and /mine explain the feature is disabled and no loot tables are seeded.
Upper bound of the per-gather quantity range for a loot row (economy_loot_tables.max_qty), paired with min_qty to define how large a single find can be.
Play-money coins credited per unit when a coin-yielding loot row is gathered (economy_loot_tables.sell_value); this is fake-economy currency only and never a real price.
Minimum tool tier that unlocks a loot row (economy_loot_tables.tool_tier): 0 is bare hands, 1 basic, 2 improved, 3 master; a member's best matching tool tier gates which drops they can roll.

Weighted odds of a single loot-table row being picked (economy_loot_tables.weight); higher weight means the item is drawn more often, so owners tune drop rarity per entry on the dashboard gathering page.

defaults.rationale: A five-minute cooldown matches the shipped code default: frequent enough to feel rewarding, spaced enough to keep the play-money economy from inflating.
Gathering is a flagship game-economy loop; per the great-defaults owner theme it ships on so the feature works out of the box, and default loot tables seed automatically on first use.
A modest common-drop stack of up to three keeps early yields satisfying without runaway play-coin gains.
Matches the seeded common drop's play-coin value: a small, steady early win that scales up with rarer, tool-gated finds.
Baseline drops start at tier 0 so a brand-new member with bare hands always gathers something; rarer rows raise the gate to reward tool investment.
Mirrors the seeded common-tier weight so the baseline everyday find dominates the roll while rarer entries stay scarce.

controls.description: Base play-money coin payout (config key economy_heist_base_payout) scaled by the randomly chosen target's payout modifier and split among the crew on success.
Seconds a guild must wait after a heist resolves before another /heist start is allowed (config key economy_heist_cooldown_seconds).
Master switch for heists (config key economy_heist_enabled); when off, /heist commands explain the feature is disabled and no heist can start or resolve.
Play-money coin cost each member pays to /heist start or /heist join (config key economy_heist_entry_fee); frozen per participant as entry_fee_paid at join time.
Seconds the recruiting window stays open for /heist join before the heist is claimed and resolved (config key economy_heist_join_window_secs).
Maximum crew size a single heist admits (config key economy_heist_max_participants); further /heist join attempts are refused as crew-full.
Minimum crew size required for a heist to attempt resolution (config key economy_heist_min_participants); below this the heist cancels and refunds every entry fee.
Single-member base success percentage (config key economy_heist_success_base_pct); the derived chance is base plus target difficulty modifier plus 7 per extra crew member, capped at 95.

defaults.rationale: A meaningful play-coin reward the target modifier scales from, giving a quick early win for a small crew and a long-term chase on the hardest targets.
A five-minute lull keeps heists a special event rather than a coin faucet, protecting the play-money economy from grind spam.
Crew heists are a flagship social game-economy loop and ship on for the maximal out-of-box experience; the stakes stay real-but-recoverable because every fee is refunded on any non-failure outcome.

A conservative, fully configurable wager that makes joining a deliberate choice without punishing casual players, and is frozen per member so a mid-window edit never changes what anyone already risked.
A minute is long enough for a guild to rally a crew and short enough to keep the tension of a live heist.
Eight is a lively crew ceiling that keeps per-person payouts meaningful; owners can widen or narrow it freely.
A heist is a crew activity; requiring at least two keeps it cooperative, and anything short of the minimum refunds everyone rather than gambling a lone member.
A balanced solo baseline: risky alone, clearly better with a bigger crew, so recruiting always feels worthwhile while staying a conservative bet.

permissions.actor: Any guild member
permissions.enforcement: Heist slash commands respond for every member; heist_start and heist_join debit and freeze the entry fee on the invoking member's own participant row, and no command lets a member act on another member's wallet or crew slot.

domains.promise: A guild crew pulls off strategic play-money heists: any member spends play-money coins to /heist start a job against a randomly chosen target, teammates /heist join within the recruiting window — each freezing the exact entry fee they paid on their own economy_heist_participants row — and once the window closes the claimed crew shares one frozen outcome. A success pays every frozen crew member the frozen per-person payout_each exactly once, a failure forfeits their entry fees, and an under-crewed or cancelled job refunds each participant their own frozen entry_fee_paid; late joins that never made the frozen crew are reconciled and refunded rather than dragged into the outcome. Every coin is play-money inside the fake game economy — never real commerce, never a market-sellable asset, and a commerce-held role earns no heist income — and money plus heist state stay idempotent under replay, crash, and concurrent join or resolve.

A light, approachable play-coin entry price that keeps a jackpot meaningful without pricing out casual members.

controls.description: Whether /pet battle is available; battles award play-money coins to the winner and pet XP to both sides.
Hours between decay cycles for the guild’s pets.
Hunger points removed from every pet each decay cycle (happiness decays at 80 percent of this rate while energy slowly recovers).
Play-money coin cost of one /pet feed.
When hunger or happiness falls to or below this value the pet turns sad; at zero it turns sick and cannot battle.
Whether the pet’s member owner receives a DM nudge when decay turns their pet sad or sick.
Whether /pet prestige is available; prestiging a level-50 pet resets it to level 1 with permanent stat bonuses.
Play-money coin cost of one /pet train session.
Master switch for companion pets; when off, decay stops and pet commands explain the feature is disabled.

defaults.rationale: Battles are a headline social feature and ship on; owners can switch the piece off independently.
Hourly cycles keep stats moving smoothly instead of in big scary jumps.
Gentle hourly decay: an unattended pet takes days, not hours, to become sad.
A light recurring coin sink that keeps care meaningful without punishing casual players.
A 20-point floor gives members a clear warning band before the pet turns sick at zero.
A single caring DM nudge is member-respectful and protects the investment members made in their pet.
Prestige gives max-level pets a long tail of progression and ships on by default.
Training doubles the feed cost so levelling stays a deliberate investment.
Companion pets are a flagship game-economy loop and ship on for the maximal out-of-box experience.

controls.description: The anti-laundering wall: when on, any item whose origin is a real-money commerce purchase (a non-tradeable item) is permanently barred from the player market; this guardrail is locked on and cannot be disabled by the owner.
Player-to-player market switch (economy_market_enabled); when off, /market subcommands reply that the market is disabled while the server shop keeps working.
Percentage market fee (economy_market_fee_pct) skimmed from each player-market sale as a play-money coin sink; the seller receives the remainder.
How many days (economy_market_listing_days) a player-market listing stays active before it expires and stops accepting buys.
Maximum simultaneously active listings (economy_market_max_listings) one member may hold on the player market.
Hard ceiling on a listing's price per unit (the MAX_PRICE_PER_UNIT guard) that rejects absurd listings well below the safe-integer limit.
Master economy switch (economy_enabled) that gates the server shop; when off, /shop, /buy, and /sell explain the economy is disabled.

defaults.rationale: Real-money items must never become a laundering path into the play-money market; the wall is locked on by design and cannot be turned off.
Player-to-player trading is a coin-movement surface, so it ships off as a deliberate guardrail until the owner opts in and sets a fee.
A light 5 percent sink keeps the market liquid while gently draining coins out of circulation.
A one-week listing window balances discoverability against stale listings clogging the board.
Ten active listings per member is generous for casual sellers while preventing one member from flooding the market.
A one-billion-coin ceiling sits far above any realistic wallet yet safely inside the JS safe-integer range, blocking absurd or overflow listings.
The server shop is the core coin sink of the game economy and ships on for the maximal out-of-box experience.

controls.description: Emoji prefix shown beside coin amounts, mapped to currency_emoji.
Display name of the play-money currency, mapped to currency_name and shown across every wallet surface.
Base play-money coins granted by /daily, mapped to economy_daily_amount; /weekly and /monthly scale from their own keys.
Master switch mapped to the economy_enabled guild_config key; when off, wallet and reward commands reply that the economy is not enabled on this server.
Conservative cap on spendable wallet coins, mapped to economy_max_wallet; zero means uncapped and a /withdraw is clamped so the wallet never exceeds a non-zero cap.
Percent tax skimmed from a /pay transfer before the receiver is credited, mapped to economy_pay_tax_pct; a conservative sink that defaults off.
Play-money coins a brand-new wallet is seeded with, mapped to economy_starting_balance and applied when economy_get_or_create_wallet first creates the row.
Percent bonus added per consecutive claim streak step, mapped to economy_streak_bonus_pct; rewards steady daily engagement without runaway payouts.

defaults.rationale: A universally readable coin emoji that owners can swap for a custom brand emoji.
A neutral, brandable default the owner can rename to match their white-label voice.
Five hundred coins is a satisfying quick early win that a casual member can claim in seconds every day.
The wallet is the backbone of the whole game economy and ships on for the maximal out-of-box experience.
Uncapped by default for a frictionless start; owners who want conservative stakes can set a real cap.
Transfers are free by default so members can share coins freely; owners can add a sink deliberately.
A zero start keeps early wins meaningful: members earn their first coins from /daily and activity rather than being handed a balance.
A gentle five percent per streak step rewards long-term consistency without letting streaks dwarf the base reward.

controls.description: Master switch for anti-raid protection; when off every join flows completely untouched.
Automatically unban members who were banned during raid mode once the raid cools down.

Graduated containment stages: stage 1 turns raid-window joiners away (kick or ban with optional message-history delete seconds), stage 2 locks down — verification raised to Very High and invites paused with settings snapshotted — if the flood persists through a stage.
Number of joins inside the sliding window that activates raid mode.
Length in seconds of the sliding join window used for flood detection.
Minimum account age while anti-raid is enabled; younger accounts are politely turned away with a DM. Zero disables the gate.
Calm minutes without threshold pressure before raid mode deactivates and every containment measure auto-reverses.
Channel for raid detection, containment, and all-clear posts; empty string falls back to the mod log channel.

defaults.rationale: Lenient locked default: no join is ever gated, deferred, or tracked until the owner deliberately opts in.
Member-respectful default: raid bans are containment, not permanent judgments, so they lift automatically with the all-clear.
Graduated locked default: start with the gentlest effective measure — reversible kicks with a respectful DM — and only lock the doors if the raid keeps coming.
Ten joins in the window is far above organic traffic for most servers, so false raid activations stay rare.
A tight ten-second window matches real raid tooling cadence without penalizing a popular invite moment.
One week filters throwaway raid accounts while barely touching genuine newcomers, who get a warm try-again-soon DM.
Five calm minutes reliably outlasts raid bursts while keeping lockdown friction short for genuine members.
Raid events fall back to the mod log until the owner dedicates a channel, so no raid is ever invisible.

controls.description: Master switch for the automod scanning pipeline; when off no rules are evaluated and configuration is preserved.
Global posture: observe logs each rule match to the mod log without acting on the member or message; enforce executes each rule’s configured action.

constraints.shape: array of { type, config, action, priority, exempt-roles, exempt-channels, log-to-mod-channel }

controls.description: Prioritized rule list; each rule carries a type (word_filter, link_filter, invite_filter, spam_filter, duplicate_filter, caps_filter, mention_spam, newline_spam), a type-specific config, an action (delete, warn, mute, kick, ban), exempt roles and channels, and a mod-log flag. Higher priority evaluates first.

Aggregate wall-clock budget for evaluating all rules — and all words within a rule — against one message; on exhaustion the remaining rules are skipped with a warning and the message is treated as clean.
Channel receiving automod detections and enforcement entries; empty string disables mod-log posts.
Hard sandboxed-VM timeout for a single owner-authored regex evaluation; a timed-out pattern is skipped and treated as no match so a slow rule can never punish a member.

defaults.rationale: Scanning on from day one gives owners visibility at zero member risk because the shipped mode is observe-only.
Lenient locked default: owners watch exactly what automod would do before any member is ever touched, then opt into enforcement deliberately.
Gentle starter set covering the highest-signal abuse shapes; under the observe default it only reports, never acts, and own-server invites stay welcome.
Aggregate cap so many rules — or many words inside one owner-editable rule — can never stall message handling; a budget bail always fails toward no match.
No mod-log channel until the owner picks one; the setup flow nudges owners to set it so observe mode has somewhere to report.
Calibrated bound: firm enough to stop catastrophic backtracking from blocking the event loop, generous enough that legitimate rules never misclassify as timeouts on a loaded host.

defaults.rationale: Guardrail against appeal spam while keeping the path genuinely open — one respectful retry per day per infraction.
Appeals land in the mod log until the owner dedicates a review channel, so no appeal is ever invisible.
Locked decision: every punishment carries an appeal path by default, reachable from both Discord and the member portal.
Member-respectful default: nobody is punished silently — every action explains itself.
Warn-before-punish locked default: two pure warnings before the first mute, graduated durations before removal, and every step DMs the member.
Forgiving 30-day memory: old mistakes fall off instead of haunting members toward escalation forever.
No mod-log channel until the owner picks one; the setup flow nudges owners to set it so escalation context is visible.

controls.description: Whether the same track URI may appear in the queue more than once. When false, duplicate additions are declined with a friendly notice.
Minutes of paused or inactive playback before the session is destroyed and the queue cleared (guild_config.music_auto_destroy_minutes).
Minutes the bot waits alone in an empty voice channel before leaving (guild_config.music_auto_leave_minutes).
Volume applied when a new queue session starts (guild_config.music_default_volume), matching the /volume command range.
Maximum total entries allowed in the guild queue; additions beyond the cap are declined with the queue-full message rather than silently trimmed.
Master switch for the music feature in the guild (guild_config.music_enabled). When false, music commands decline politely with an owner-branded notice.
Maximum queued entries a single member may hold at once (not counting the playing track), preventing queue monopolization.

defaults.rationale: Member-respectful default: repeat requests are a normal part of shared listening; owners who dislike repeats can turn it off.
Matches the shipped default: thirty minutes of inactivity before the session and queue are cleaned up.
Matches the shipped default: five minutes alone in voice before leaving balances persistence with not squatting in channels.
Matches the shipped dashboard and bot default of 50, a comfortable mid-level that respects listeners on first use.
Matches the enforced storage guardrail of five thousand entries, well within the serialized-state budget.
Owner theme: every feature works perfectly out of the box; music is live the moment the bot joins.
Matches the enforced per-user guardrail of fifty entries so no single member monopolizes the collaborative queue.

controls.description: Discord role id granting DJ arbitration powers (force-skip, /stop, /volume, /loop, /shuffle, /seek, /remove, /pause, /filter). Empty string means no DJ role is configured and arbitration falls back to the guild owner only. Set via the dashboard Music page (guild_config.dj_role_id).

When true, members can cast priority votes on upcoming queue entries; entries with more priority votes are promoted ahead of same-requester entries with fewer votes, never displacing the currently playing track.
When true, a member can reposition their own queued (not yet played) tracks within the queue; moving or removing another member's track still requires the DJ role.
When true, the requester of the currently playing track can skip it instantly with /skip, without a vote and without the DJ role.
Percentage of non-bot listeners in the voice channel whose votes are required for a vote-skip of another member's track to pass. Votes needed = ceil(listeners * threshold / 100).

defaults.rationale: Owner decision: the DJ role is optional arbitration, not a prerequisite. Out of the box no DJ role exists and fairness is governed by self-skip plus listener-majority voting.
Owner decision: voting-based priority is part of the fairness model and is on by default so popular picks rise without DJ intervention.
Owner decision: requesters manage their own queued tracks. Members keep agency over their own picks without needing DJ powers.
Owner decision: you can always skip your own track. This is the member-respectful default and stays on unless the owner deliberately disables it.
Owner decision: listener-majority vote-skip. 50 percent with ceiling rounding reproduces ceil(listeners / 2), a simple majority of humans in the voice channel.

permissions.action: Force-skip another member's currently playing track without a vote

permissions.enforcement: The /skip handler routes non-requester non-DJ invocations into the vote-skip tally; no immediate skip occurs until the listener-majority threshold is met.

permissions.action: Move or remove another member's queued track

permissions.action: Reposition their own entry within the upcoming queue

permissions.enforcement: The /play handler only requires voice-channel presence and a text channel; no role gate is applied before queueing.

permissions.action: Instantly skip their own currently playing track with /skip
permissions.actor: The member who requested the currently playing track
permissions.enforcement: The /skip handler compares the invoking user id to the current entry's requestedBy and bypasses both the vote and the DJ check on match while self-skip-enabled is true.

domains.promise: Any member can queue tracks with /play; a requester can always instantly skip their own currently playing track; skipping anyone else's track requires a listener-majority vote among the humans in the voice channel; an optional dashboard-configured DJ role adds arbitration powers (force-skip, stop, volume, filters, remove); a requester can reposition their own queued tracks; and queue priority can be raised by member votes. All fairness rules are enforced per guild with owner-branded messaging.

permissions.enforcement: Fraud API routes return 401/403 to non-admin sessions and RLS blocks direct table reads; the staff channel is the only Discord surface and only if the owner configured one.

permissions.action: View and resolve fraud signals and incidents via the dashboard fraud page and /api/fraud/signals
permissions.actor: Guild owner or dashboard admin
permissions.enforcement: The fraud routes require an authenticated owner/admin session with guild scoping on every read and status change.

domains.promise: Commerce is watched continuously: purchase velocity, device abuse, IP mismatch, and failed-payment patterns raise fraud signals that are mirrored to the dashboard fraud queue and the configured staff channel, critical signals DM the owner directly, and bursts of critical signals auto-open a deduplicated incident — all without ever blocking a legitimate purchase on detector failure.

assertions.expectedObservation: The owner DM arrives for the critical signal naming severity, type, and guild; no member-visible channel mentions fraud.
fraud_signals holds one velocity row per threshold crossing with evidence fields (order count, window, threshold) and open status.
Signal creation is traceable with the triggering customer and evidence snapshot.
The dashboard fraud queue lists the signals with severity badges matching the thresholds.
The owner DM uses the branded alert template in the owner's voice.
Re-evaluating the same order set does not append duplicate signals for the same crossing.
Run signals are resolved and swept with evidence retention honored.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: Driving five run-prefixed orders for one test customer within the window creates one velocity signal with order-count evidence; driving ten creates a critical signal and the owner receives the critical DM.
scenarios.promise: Out of the box, five orders by one customer inside an hour raises a velocity signal with evidence, visible in the dashboard fraud queue, and a critical-severity signal DMs the owner.

assertions.expectedObservation: Owner notification behavior matches the recomputed severity for the lowered threshold.
The signal's evidence records threshold 2 and order count 2, and the rules row shows the configured value.
The rule change and the resulting signal are both audited in order.
The dashboard rules page shows the new threshold and the queue shows the earlier-firing signal.
Alert copy reflects the configured values accurately without stale defaults.
Re-running detection under the new rule does not duplicate the signal.
The rule reverts to default and run signals sweep clean.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: With the threshold configured to 2, two orders by one customer create a velocity signal citing the configured threshold in its evidence; a control customer with one order raises nothing.
scenarios.promise: Threshold configuration takes effect: lowering velocity-order-threshold to 2 makes the detector fire on the second order in the window.

assertions.expectedObservation: The staff channel receives exactly one mirror per signal with type, severity, and entity kind only.
The config row holds the staff channel id and the signal row is unchanged by mirroring.
The channel configuration and each mirror post are traceable.
Owner DM for critical signals continues alongside the staff mirror without duplication.
The staff alert uses the branded template and directs staff to the dashboard for evidence.
Replayed signal processing posts no duplicate staff mirror for the same signal.
Staff channel messages and the channel config are removed in the sweep.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: After configuring a private staff channel, a triggered signal posts the staff-channel-alert there while the dashboard row and (for critical) owner DM still occur; the message contains no card, amount, or personal payment data.
scenarios.promise: Staff-channel configuration takes effect: with staff-alert-channel set, every new signal mirrors to that channel naming type, severity, and entity kind — never buyer payment details.

assertions.expectedObservation: No alert behavior changes result from the rejected submissions.
The rules rows are byte-identical before and after each rejected mutation.
Each rejected rule change is logged with its validation reason.
The dashboard rules form shows precise field-level errors to the owner.
Validation errors are clean branded copy without internals.
Resubmitting invalid rules repeatedly changes nothing.
Zero residue from the rejected submissions is confirmed.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: PUT /api/fraud/rules with a zero velocity threshold, a non-numeric channel id, and an unknown rule key each return validation errors; the rules rows are unchanged and a subsequent detection run uses the prior thresholds.
scenarios.promise: Invalid rule configuration is rejected atomically: negative or zero thresholds, malformed channel ids, and unknown signal types never persist and the previous rules keep running.

assertions.expectedObservation: No fraud content is visible to the member account anywhere in the guild.
RLS returns zero fraud rows to the anon client and the denied API calls changed nothing.
The denied reads and writes are logged with caller identity.
Repeated unauthorized probing of fraud surfaces itself feeds the security signal path.
Denial responses are minimal branded envelopes.
Replayed denied requests never escalate access.
The denial run leaves zero residue.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: A member-session GET on /api/fraud/signals and PUT on /api/fraud/rules return 401/403 with no data; anon RLS probes on fraud tables return nothing; a member cannot see the staff channel absent explicit channel permission.
scenarios.promise: Fraud data is admin-only: member sessions cannot read signals or incidents, cannot tune rules, and no fraud detail reaches member-visible Discord surfaces.

assertions.expectedObservation: The buyer's purchase, receipt, and roles are entirely unaffected by the detector outage.
Order, payment, and entitlement rows are complete despite the failed signal insert.
The signal-write failure is recorded as fraud.signal_write_failed with its cause.
The owner receives the detector-failure notice per the critical-failures-DM-owners decision.
The failure notice is branded and states that commerce continued safely.
Recovery re-evaluation does not double-signal the same historical crossing.
Outage-era run artifacts sweep clean with audit retained.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: With fraud_signals writes made to fail, a purchase that would trigger velocity completes normally end to end; the detector failure is surfaced to the owner as a critical operational notice and detection resumes after recovery.
scenarios.promise: Detector failure never blocks commerce: when signal persistence fails, the triggering purchase still completes, and the detector failure itself reaches the owner.

assertions.expectedObservation: The staff mirror posted despite the DM failure, and a later critical signal DMs the owner successfully.
The signal row was never dropped or downgraded by the notification failure.
fraud.owner_dm_failed is recorded with the retry outcome traceable.
The dashboard queue remained the authoritative surface throughout.
Retried notifications render identically to first-try ones.
The retry never double-DMs a signal that already notified successfully.
Run signals and messages sweep to zero residue.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: With the owner's DMs temporarily closed, a critical signal keeps its dashboard row and staff mirror; after DMs reopen, the next critical notification cycle reaches the owner and the earlier failure is visible in the trail.
scenarios.promise: Transient notification failures converge: a failed owner DM or staff mirror is retried so the finding is never silently lost.

assertions.expectedObservation: Owner DM and staff channel message counts are unchanged by all replays.
Signal and incident row counts are identical before and after replay.
Replay evaluations appear as no-ops without duplicating signal-creation entries.
The dashboard queue shows the same finding set with no replay inflation.
No replay artifact surfaces anywhere user-visible.
Signal identity and the unresolved-incident dedupe provably fence duplicate creation.
The single finding footprint sweeps clean.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: Replaying the webhook and activation events behind an existing signal set leaves fraud_signals, incidents, owner DMs, and staff mirrors count-identical.
scenarios.promise: Detection is replay-safe: re-processing the same commerce events, or re-delivering the events that fed the detectors, never duplicates signals, incidents, or notifications.

assertions.expectedObservation: Post-restart critical signals still DM the owner; no restart-era finding was lost or re-announced.
Signal and incident rows are byte-identical across the restart.
The trail is continuous with no restart gap.
The dashboard queue and incidents page render the pre-restart findings on first load.
Post-restart alerts render identical branding.
Restart-era event redeliveries are absorbed without duplicate findings.
Pre-restart findings sweep clean post-restart.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: With one open signal and one open incident, the stack restarts; both remain open with evidence intact, the dashboard renders them immediately, and a new triggering event after boot raises a fresh signal normally.
scenarios.promise: Findings survive restart: open signals and incidents persist across a full stack restart and detection resumes on the next commerce event.

assertions.expectedObservation: The owner receives one incident-opened notification, not one per racing evaluation.
One incidents row with source fraud_auto exists for the burst, its number drawn from the atomic sequence.
The incident's auto-created event records the burst count once; racing evaluations are visible as dedupe hits.
The incidents page shows a single consolidated incident for the burst.
The single incident notice is branded and states the burst size.
Later evaluations inside the window continue attaching to the open incident rather than opening another.
The incident is resolved and swept with its timeline retained per policy.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: Three critical signals landing concurrently produce exactly one auto-created incident with a unique incident number; the racing evaluations observe the existing unresolved incident and attach rather than duplicate.
scenarios.promise: Concurrent critical bursts are safe: simultaneous critical signals crossing the incident threshold create exactly one incident via the atomic incident sequence and dedupe check.

assertions.expectedObservation: Only guild A's owner and staff channel receive alerts; guild B's surfaces are silent.
All signal and incident rows carry guild A's id and are RLS-invisible to guild B admins.
Audit rows are exclusively guild A scoped.
Guild B's fraud queue and incident list contain nothing from the run.
Guild A's alerts use guild A's brand configuration.
Replaying guild A's triggering events cannot create findings in guild B.
Sweeping guild A leaves guild B byte-identical.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: Triggering signals in guild A produces zero fraud rows scoped to guild B, no message in guild B's staff channel, and no DM to guild B's owner; guild B's fraud queue stays empty.
scenarios.promise: Fraud isolation is per guild: guild A's signals, incidents, and alerts never appear in guild B's dashboard, staff channel, or owner DMs.

assertions.expectedObservation: Run alert messages are removed from the staff channel and no test DMs remain actionable.
Zero run-prefixed open signals or incidents remain.
Signal and incident audit history remains append-only and undeleted.
The fraud queue and incidents page are empty of test artifacts post-sweep.
Rule and channel configuration are restored to pre-run values.
A second cleanup pass is an error-free no-op.
The sweep report enumerates every created fraud artifact and confirms removal or intentional retention.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: The cleanup pass resolves and removes run-prefixed fraud artifacts across Discord and Supabase, restores default rules, and a verification sweep returns zero operational residue with the audit trail intact.
scenarios.promise: The domain cleans up: run-prefixed signals, incidents, staff alerts, and rule changes are resolved and removed, while evidence and audit history follow the retention policy rather than being destroyed.

transitions.expectedEffect: The triggering commerce operation completes normally; the detector failure itself is surfaced to the owner and retried.

transitions.expectedEffect: Exactly one incident is created for the burst via the atomic incident sequence, with an auto-created event and owner notification.
transitions.trigger: Open critical signals within one hour reach the incident threshold

transitions.trigger: A detector threshold is crossed (velocity, device abuse, IP mismatch, or payment pattern)

transitions.expectedEffect: Detection resumes; events that occurred during degradation are re-evaluated on their next observable action.
transitions.trigger: The failed dependency recovers

transitions.expectedEffect: The incident closes with its event timeline intact for later audit.
transitions.trigger: Owner resolves the incident after review

transitions.expectedEffect: The signal closes with resolution noted; evidence rows are retained, never deleted.

values.description: A detector or its persistence failed; commerce continues unblocked while the failure is surfaced and retried.
A critical burst consolidated into a single auto-created incident with its event timeline.
Detectors run on every purchase, activation, validation, and payment event with no open findings.
Signals and incidents were reviewed and resolved by the owner or staff; evidence is retained.

controls.description: Expected interval between SDK heartbeats; sessions missing heartbeats beyond a multiple of this interval stop counting toward the device limit.
Brand prefix on generated keys (format PREFIX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX); part of the product's white-label surface.
Per-product default for how many concurrent device sessions one license key may hold before new activations are refused until a slot is freed.
What happens when a buyer asks to recover a key: rotate-and-invalidate issues a fresh key and kills the old one immediately; reveal-existing is never offered because plaintext keys are not stored.
Lets the key holder sign out individual devices from the portal (and via /api/license/deactivate on uninstall) without contacting the owner.
Keys are persisted as SHA-256 hashes with only prefix and suffix retained for display; the full key exists in plaintext only in the one-time issuance message.

defaults.rationale: Hourly heartbeats keep session liveness fresh without burdening client apps or the API.
Matches the shipped generator's SMNI-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX format; owners may rebrand the prefix per product.
Three devices covers a desktop, laptop, and spare for a single honest buyer while keeping sharing visible to fraud detection.
Owner decision: recovery is rotation, never reveal — the old key dies instantly and the new one is shown once.
Portal self-service decision: buyers free their own device slots without support round-trips.
Hashed-only storage means a database leak cannot leak usable keys; this is a hard security default.

evidence.expectedObservation: Activation, refusal, and status surfaces behave exactly as contracted with masked key display only.
evidence.observer: Discord test client driving /license activate, check, and info with bound and foreign accounts

evidence.expectedObservation: Only hashes exist at rest (with prefix/suffix), sessions respect the device limit, and RLS hides key rows from non-service clients.
evidence.observer: Supabase service client inspecting license_keys, license_sessions, and entitlements plus anon-client probes

evidence.expectedObservation: Every activation, rotation, device change, and revocation leaves an append-only audit row.
evidence.observer: audit_logs reader filtered to key.activated, rotation, session, and revocation actions

evidence.expectedObservation: Unresolved role delivery and abuse patterns surface to the owner; healthy key activity stays quiet.
evidence.observer: Owner DM inbox, alerts table, and the dashboard licenses page

evidence.expectedObservation: Key surfaces carry the owner brand and configured key prefix with powered-by-SomniBot attribution.
evidence.observer: Snapshot comparer over activation embeds, portal license pages, and generated key prefixes

evidence.expectedObservation: No replayed operation double-grants roles, issues extra keys, or exceeds the device limit.
evidence.observer: Duplicate-request driver replaying activations, rotations, and device operations while counting grants

evidence.expectedObservation: All run-prefixed license resources are removed while audit history remains.
evidence.observer: Post-run sweeper over run-prefixed keys, sessions, and granted roles

failures.expectedBehavior: Activation and entitlement state stay consistent; role delivery is reconciled through the durable commerce delivery intent instead of being silently dropped, and unresolved delivery surfaces to the owner.

failures.expectedBehavior: Exactly one new key is issued; the losing request observes the completed rotation and no second key is generated or revealed.

failures.expectedBehavior: Client apps keep last-known-good entitlement until the next successful heartbeat; no key state mutates and no session is dropped by the outage alone.
failures.trigger: POST /api/license/validate is unreachable or returns 5xx

domains.name: License keys

permissions.action: Activate the key with /license activate and receive the product's roles and entitlement
permissions.actor: The Discord account the key was issued to (bound_discord_id)
permissions.enforcement: The handler hashes the submitted key, looks it up guild-scoped, and verifies bound_discord_id equals the invoker before any state change.

permissions.action: Activate, inspect, or benefit from someone else's key
permissions.actor: Any Discord account other than the bound owner
permissions.enforcement: Bound-account mismatch returns the key-bound-elsewhere refusal with zero state change; key details are never disclosed to the caller.

permissions.action: Run /license info <key> to view masked key details, status, and active sessions
permissions.actor: Guild administrator
permissions.enforcement: The subcommand requires the Administrator permission and displays the key only in masked prefix/suffix form.

permissions.action: List sessions, remove a device, and deactivate on uninstall for their own keys
permissions.actor: Authenticated key holder in the customer portal or via the license SDK
permissions.enforcement: Portal session token and license-key proof scope every session read/write to the holder's own keys; rate limits protect the endpoints.

permissions.action: Run /license info
permissions.actor: Guild member without Administrator permission
permissions.enforcement: The handler replies admin-only and performs no lookup.

domains.promise: License keys are secure by construction and self-serviceable: keys are stored only as hashes (SMNI-prefixed, shown in full exactly once at issuance), activation via /license activate binds strictly to the purchasing Discord account, compromised keys are rotated — never revealed — and buyers manage their own device sessions within the configured device limit through the portal and license SDK endpoints.

assertions.expectedObservation: /license activate replies with the activation-success embed listing granted roles, and /license check shows the active entitlement with expiry formatting.
license_keys holds key_hash, key_prefix, and key_suffix but no plaintext key; the key and entitlement rows are active and guild-scoped.
key.activated is audited with actor, key id, product, and granted role ids.
The dashboard licenses page lists the key as active with its masked display; no alert fires.
The key carries the configured prefix and the activation embed uses the owner brand with powered-by attribution.
Running /license activate again returns already-active with no second role grant or audit duplication.
The run key, sessions, entitlement, and roles sweep to zero residue with audit retained.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: A run-prefixed purchase issues a pending SMNI key; the bound buyer activates it, roles land, /license check lists the active entitlement, and the database holds only the key hash with prefix/suffix.
scenarios.promise: Out of the box, a purchased license activates for its bound buyer with /license activate, grants the product roles, and appears in /license check — with the key stored only as a hash.

assertions.expectedObservation: No Discord-side state changes from device churn; the holder's roles and entitlement remain stable throughout.
license_sessions never exceeds one active row for the key; the removed session is marked inactive rather than deleted.
The refused bind, the self-service removal, and the successful rebind are each audited.
The dashboard license detail shows the current single session and the config value of 1.
The device-limit-reached copy names the configured limit and points to the owner-branded portal.
Replaying device B's refused validate never sneaks a second concurrent session in.
Run sessions and the config change sweep clean afterward.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: With max-devices configured to 1 for the product, device A validates and binds; device B is refused with device-limit-reached; after the holder removes device A in the portal, device B binds successfully.
scenarios.promise: Device-limit configuration takes effect: with max-devices set to 1, a second device is refused until the holder frees the slot through portal self-service.

assertions.expectedObservation: /license activate with the old key returns invalid-key; the entitlement and roles persist uninterrupted through rotation.
The old key hash is invalidated, the new hash is live, and at no time did a plaintext key column or log row exist.
The rotation is audited linking old and new key ids without recording either plaintext.
The dashboard shows the key's rotation history with masked displays only.
The rotation notice uses the key-rotated template with product name and new key tail in the owner's voice.
Replaying the rotation request returns the completed rotation instead of minting further keys.
Both key generations are swept with the rotation audit retained.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: The holder rotates their key in the portal; the new key displays once, its hash replaces the old binding, the old key fails /license activate and SDK validate immediately, and no API response anywhere contains the old plaintext.
scenarios.promise: Rotation configuration takes effect: rotate-and-invalidate issues a new key shown exactly once and kills the old key immediately, with no path that reveals a stored key.

assertions.expectedObservation: Each attempt gets the same ephemeral invalid-key embed, leaking no distinction an attacker could use to probe key space.
license_keys, entitlements, and sessions are unchanged by every rejected attempt.
Failed activation attempts are logged with the hashed submission for abuse analysis, never the raw guess in plaintext beyond hashing.
Repeated failed attempts feed the fraud domain's signals rather than raising per-attempt alarms.
Refusal copy stays friendly and branded with no technical detail.
Unlimited retries of invalid keys accumulate no state beyond rate-limit counters.
Nothing was created; the sweep confirms zero residue.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: Activation attempts with a malformed string, a well-formed but nonexistent key, and a valid key against the wrong guild each return the invalid-key refusal; no lookup response distinguishes which failure occurred beyond the safe message.
scenarios.promise: Malformed and unknown keys are rejected safely: bad formats and nonexistent keys produce friendly refusals with zero state change and no information leak about real keys.

assertions.expectedObservation: The foreign account sees key-bound-elsewhere and the non-admin sees the admin-only refusal; the bound buyer's state is untouched.
No key, session, or entitlement row changed, and RLS blocks the foreign account's direct reads of the key row.
The denied foreign activation and denied info call are logged with caller identities.
Foreign-activation attempts are visible to the owner through the security/fraud surfaces, not silent.
Denial messages are branded and reveal nothing about the key's true owner.
Repeating the denied attempts cannot escalate access or lock out the legitimate holder.
Zero residue from the denial run is confirmed by the sweep.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: A second test account submitting the buyer's key gets key-bound-elsewhere with zero state change; the same account running /license info gets the admin-only refusal with no lookup performed.
scenarios.promise: Binding and admin gates hold: a foreign account cannot activate someone else's key, and a non-admin cannot use /license info.

assertions.expectedObservation: The holder's roles and entitlement are untouched by the outage.
license_sessions rows are unchanged during the outage and refreshed, not duplicated, on recovery.
The outage window is recorded as license.validate_unavailable with recovery visible in the trail.
Sustained validation failure raises one deduped owner alert; a blip raises none.
The degraded response copy reassures the customer their activation keeps working.
Queued client retries from the outage window are absorbed without session duplication.
Run sessions sweep clean with the outage audit retained.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: With /api/license/validate made unreachable, an SDK client with a live session continues under validate-degraded semantics; after recovery the next heartbeat reconciles the session with no state loss and no duplicate session row.
scenarios.promise: Validation-service failure fails safe for paying customers: when the validate endpoint is down, existing activations keep working on last-known-good and no session is dropped by the outage.

assertions.expectedObservation: After convergence the member holds each contracted role exactly once.
The delivery intent row shows the failed attempt and its settled resolution; entitlement state never flapped.
The transient failure and reconciliation are both traceable in the audit trail.
A quickly-reconciled delivery raises no owner alert; only stuck intents would.
The buyer-facing activation message never exposed the transient hiccup.
The retry path cannot double-add roles thanks to the delivery intent's mutation fencing.
Intent rows and roles from the run sweep to zero residue.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: With an induced transient Discord API failure on the first role add, activation completes, the delivery intent records the unresolved role, and reconciliation converges the member to exactly the granted role set with the intent settled.
scenarios.promise: Transient activation failures converge: a role grant that fails once during activation is reconciled by the durable delivery machinery to the exact contracted role set.

assertions.expectedObservation: Role state and DM counts are identical before and after all replays.
Key, session, and entitlement row counts are unchanged by every replay.
Replays appear as no-op entries without duplicating the original transition rows.
The dashboard shows single entries per real operation with no replay artifacts.
Replay responses reuse the friendly already-done copy rather than errors.
Status-guarded transitions and hashed-key uniqueness provably fence every duplicate path.
The single-operation footprint sweeps clean.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: Replaying /license activate returns already-active with unchanged rows; replaying a device deactivate is a no-op on the already-inactive session; replaying the rotation confirmation returns the existing rotation without minting keys.
scenarios.promise: Key operations are replay-safe: repeated activation, repeated deactivation of the same device, and repeated rotation confirmations never duplicate grants, sessions, or keys.

assertions.expectedObservation: Post-restart activation and check commands work on first invocation with correct state.
Session rows and key statuses are byte-identical across the restart apart from refreshed heartbeat timestamps.
The audit trail is continuous across the restart with no gap or duplicate transitions.
No spurious alerts fire from the restart.
Post-restart surfaces render identical owner branding.
Client retries spanning the restart window are absorbed idempotently.
Run resources created before the restart sweep clean after it.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: With one active key holding sessions and one pending key, bot and dashboard restart; the active key's SDK heartbeat succeeds immediately, the pending key activates normally, and no session was lost or duplicated.
scenarios.promise: Key and session state survive restart: active keys, device sessions, and pending activations behave identically after the full stack restarts.

assertions.expectedObservation: One activation success and one already-active reply; roles granted exactly once.
Session count never exceeds the device limit under concurrency, enforced at the database rather than in bot memory.
Both racers are logged with their outcomes and the winning transition appears once.
The license detail shows a consistent final state with no phantom session.
The losing device receives the branded device-limit-reached message, not an error dump.
Late retries from the losing racer remain fenced by the same guards.
The single-winner footprint sweeps to zero residue.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: Two parallel /license activate calls yield one activation and one already-active reply with a single role grant; two devices racing for the final session slot yield exactly one new session and one device-limit refusal.
scenarios.promise: Concurrent key operations are safe: simultaneous activations of one key, and simultaneous device binds competing for the last slot, resolve to exactly one winner with clean refusals.

assertions.expectedObservation: Activation in guild B is refused with invalid-key while the same key still works in guild A.
The key lookup is guild-scoped so guild B queries return nothing, and RLS keeps guild A's key rows invisible to guild B admins.
The cross-guild attempt is logged under guild B without referencing guild A's key identity.
Neither owner receives cross-guild noise from the attempt.
Each guild's refusal and success copy uses its own brand configuration.
Repeated cross-guild attempts never leak or bind the key outside its home guild.
Sweeping guild A's key leaves guild B byte-identical.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: The bound buyer running /license activate with their guild-A key inside guild B receives invalid-key; guild B's licenses dashboard and database scope contain nothing, and guild A's key state is untouched.
scenarios.promise: Keys are guild-scoped: a key issued in guild A cannot be activated, inspected, or validated in guild B, and guild B sees no trace of it.

assertions.expectedObservation: Test roles granted through activations are removed from all test accounts.
Zero run-prefixed rows remain in license_keys, license_sessions, or delivery-intent tables.
Activation, rotation, and revocation audit rows remain append-only and undeleted.
The licenses dashboard shows no lingering test keys after the sweep.
Any key-prefix or device-limit configuration changed during scenarios is restored.
Running the cleanup twice is an error-free no-op the second time.
The sweep report enumerates every created key and session and confirms removal or intentional retention.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: The cleanup pass removes all run-prefixed license resources across Discord and Supabase, and a verification sweep returns zero operational residue with audit rows intact.
scenarios.promise: The domain cleans up: run-prefixed keys, sessions, delivery intents, and granted roles are removed, while activation and rotation audit history is preserved.

values.description: Key activated; entitlement active, roles granted, device sessions may bind up to the limit.
All device slots are occupied; new devices are refused until the holder frees a slot.
Key issued at fulfillment, hash stored, bound to the buyer, awaiting /license activate.
Entitlement revocation (refund, cancellation, expiry) shut this key down and terminated its sessions.
Key replaced by rotation; this key hash is invalid forever and its successor carries the entitlement.

controls.description: Accepts refund events against historical subscription sale payments whose currency label was persisted as a hardcoded USD, matching on exact evidence before tolerating the label mismatch.
Days a subscription entitlement stays in grace_period after a failed payment before automatic revocation, giving PayPal dunning time to recover the charge.
Which PayPal API base the stack talks to; the proof suite always runs against sandbox and live is an explicit owner cutover.
Order of operations for owner-initiated refunds: provider-first confirms the PayPal refund outcome before local entitlement and payment state flip; local-first is not offered for money paths.
Age after which a webhook event stuck in processing (for example from a crash) may be reclaimed and resumed by a new delivery.
Maximum signature verification attempts per delivery (one initial call plus quick retries) before the route answers 503 so PayPal redelivers.

defaults.rationale: Historical sale rows were persisted with a hardcoded USD label; refusing their refunds would strand real customer money, so the tolerance ships on with exact-evidence matching.
Matches the shipped suspension default: three days of retained access covers typical PayPal payment retry cycles without extending free access indefinitely.
Every automated proof runs against PayPal sandbox; switching to live is a deliberate owner action, never a default.
Owner decision: never flip local money state until PayPal has confirmed the refund, so the ledger can never claim money moved that did not.
Five minutes matches the shipped stale-processing constant: long enough for slow handlers, short enough that crashed events resume on the next redelivery.
Matches the shipped verification budget: one call plus two quick retries fits inside the webhook time budget while riding out API blips.

controls.description: When a self-service cancellation takes effect: end-of-term keeps paid access until the current period ends; immediate revokes on confirmation.
Lifetime of an HMAC-signed download URL issued by /api/portal/download-link; expired links are refused and a fresh one must be requested.
Whether the portal chrome (name, logo, colors) derives from the guild profile or a custom owner brand kit.
Lifetime of a portal session token from Discord OAuth sign-in; expired sessions require a fresh sign-in.
Lets a buyer file a refund request from an order's portal page; the request lands in the owner's dashboard queue and never auto-refunds.
Lets a subscriber cancel their own subscription from the portal without contacting the owner.
Lets a buyer of a ticket-fulfilled service product open a service request thread from the portal.

defaults.rationale: Owner decision: cancellation is end-of-term by default — buyers keep what they paid for and are simply not billed again.
Five minutes matches the shipped signed-URL expiry: ample for a click, useless to a link leaker.
White-label decision: the portal is the owner's storefront back-office for buyers and must never look like a third-party site.
Seven days matches the shipped session lifetime: convenient for buyers while keeping stolen-token exposure bounded.
A visible refund path is member-respectful and routes disputes to the owner instead of the payment processor.
Portal self-service decision: buyers control their own subscriptions without support friction.
Ticket-fulfilled service products need a first-class request channel out of the box.

domains.name: Customer portal

permissions.action: Obtain a portal session and view their own purchase data
permissions.actor: Any Discord user completing OAuth who matches a customer record for the guild
permissions.enforcement: POST /api/portal/auth exchanges the OAuth code with Discord, matches /users/@me against the customers table, and issues a hashed session token bound to that customer.

permissions.action: Read or mutate any other customer's orders, keys, sessions, or requests
permissions.actor: Authenticated portal customer
permissions.enforcement: Customer scoping is applied server-side from the session binding — client-supplied customer or order ids outside the binding return 404/403 and RLS blocks direct table access.

permissions.action: List their own orders, subscriptions, licenses, sessions, and downloads
permissions.actor: Authenticated portal customer
permissions.enforcement: Every portal API verifies the x-portal-token hash, resolves the bound customer, and scopes all queries to that customer id; reads are rate-limited per token.

permissions.action: Rotate their own keys, remove their own devices, schedule cancellation, and file refund or service requests
permissions.actor: Authenticated portal customer
permissions.enforcement: Each action verifies the target resource belongs to the session's customer and records the action with an idempotency identity.

domains.promise: Buyers self-serve everything about their purchases in an owner-branded portal: Discord OAuth sign-in, re-downloading files via short-lived signed links, license key rotation and device controls, live order and subscription state, end-of-term cancellation, and refund or service requests — all strictly scoped to the signed-in customer's own data.

controls.description: Minimum seconds between automation-sent DMs to the same member from the same automation.

Global cap on automation fires per member per minute, enforced atomically in Valkey.

defaults.rationale: Matches AUTOMATION_LIMITS.DM_COOLDOWN_SECONDS; members are never DM-flooded by rules.
A single occurrence touching more than 25 members is almost never intended; holding it protects against harmful loops and compromised admins.
Matches AUTOMATION_LIMITS.MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH; three hops covers legitimate cascades while cutting loops fast.
Owner decision: rules preview their resolved actions before going live so surprises happen in the preview, not in the server.
Matches AUTOMATION_LIMITS.MAX_FIRES_PER_USER_PER_MINUTE; generous for real activity, hostile to spam.

controls.description: Per-product feature flag strings delivered through the validation protocol for in-project capability gating.
Server-directed heartbeat cadence returned by validation; the generated contract requires a conforming integration to clamp any interval below 30 seconds up to 30 to protect the API.
Per-product license delivery mode string (dashboard PUT /api/license/config/[productId], max 32 chars); portal_only is the canonical shipped mode where keys are surfaced through the customer portal.
Maximum concurrent active device sessions per license key; enforced atomically by the license_validate_device RPC at validation time.
How long a device may keep operating on its cached validation while the license server is unreachable, measured on a server-time-anchored monotonic clock.
Whether validation requires the bound customer to still be a member of the product's Discord guild.
How long a conforming generated integration may serve a cached valid response before revalidating; always capped at a payment-grace deadline when one is in force.

defaults.rationale: No flags until the owner defines them; the validation protocol returns an empty list rather than an absent field.
Five-minute heartbeats keep session truth fresh without meaningful API load; matches the API default.
Keys are account-bound and reached through the branded customer portal by default; matches the route-level default in /api/license/config.
Three devices covers a customer's desktop, laptop, and spare without inviting key sharing; matches the API default.
A 24-hour offline window is member-respectful for flaky connections while the server-side heartbeat system remains the authoritative enforcement.
Products are community goods; leaving the guild ends entitlement checks by default, and owners can relax this per product.
One minute of integration-side caching absorbs bursts while keeping revocations fast; matches the generated contract default.

domains.name: Generated SomniBot licensing contract and validation protocol

permissions.action: Read, enumerate, or revoke another guild's license keys, sessions, or customer PII
permissions.actor: Owner of an unrelated guild
permissions.enforcement: All admin lookups are constrained to the caller's guild_id (V47-C2); cross-guild UUID or hash guesses return not-found, never data.

permissions.action: View their own license keys and device sessions, and free a device slot from the portal
permissions.actor: Customer holding a valid portal token
permissions.enforcement: x-portal-token is hash-matched against unexpired, unrevoked portal_sessions and rate limited; data is filtered to the token's customer_id only.

permissions.action: List device sessions (GET /api/license/sessions) and revoke one (DELETE /api/license/sessions/[id]) as a recovery reset
permissions.actor: Guild owner in the dashboard
permissions.enforcement: requireGuildOwner plus a parent license_keys.guild_id ownership check on every session operation; revocation marks the session inactive with reason admin_revoked.

permissions.action: POST /api/license/validate, /api/license/heartbeat, and /api/license/deactivate
permissions.actor: Any external app presenting a license key
permissions.enforcement: Public endpoints protected by per-IP and per-key-hash rate limits; keys are stored and compared only as SHA-256 hashes; every attempt is logged to license_validations.

domains.promise: A self-contained SomniBot licensing contract generated for the customer's existing project defines the validate, heartbeat, and deactivate protocol against the dashboard license API. A conforming integration validates license keys for real-store products against hashed key storage, enforces per-product device limits through atomic session registration, keeps sessions honest with heartbeats, honors a bounded offline grace window on a monotonic clock without ever extending a lapsed payment-grace deadline, and gives the owner and customer working recovery resets that free device slots — all strictly guild-scoped and replay-safe. License access is account-bound commerce state and never touches the play-money game economy.
